1858 – Habits de Lumière

Projection Mapping · Architectural
2022
Graphics eMotion
Épernay, France

An architectural projection mapping production using the Hôtel de Ville itself to carry the story of its history and reconstruction.

Role
Projection Mapping Artist
Tools
Cinema 4DAfter EffectsPhotoshop
Overview

Created by Graphics eMotion for Habits de Lumière 2022 in Épernay, the 15-minute show followed the building’s history through the voice of architect Victor Lenoir. My contribution covered several sequences combining lighting, particles, compositing and motion design within the studio’s larger production.

My Contribution
  • Prepared projection mapping layouts for the façade geometry.
  • Developed assigned scenes through lighting, shading, particles and compositing.
  • Designed motion at a scale and rhythm appropriate for architectural viewing.
  • Integrated the sequences within the studio’s broader narrative and technical framework.

I contributed multiple projection mapping sequences to the show as part of the Graphics eMotion team; the overall show — direction, narration, staging and other sequences — was a full studio production, not a solo work.

Pipeline
  • Façade mapping preparation
  • Narrative scene development
  • Lighting and particle integration
  • Distance-readability review
  • Compositing and show integration
Technical Challenges
  • Challenge — every visual event had to align with the façade while remaining clear at long viewing distances.
  • Production response — architectural lines guided composition, lighting and particle movement, with projection accuracy reviewed alongside narrative rhythm.
  • Production impact — the assigned sequences supported the historical story without separating the imagery from the building that carried it.
Design Intent

The façade was treated as part of the narration rather than a neutral screen. Composition and movement followed the building’s structure so historical and poetic moments remained readable from the public viewing distance.

Project Impact

The finished show used large-scale projection to connect the Hôtel de Ville’s architecture with the history being narrated across its façade.
